title: Analysis of Lysophagic Flux in Cultured Cells using Lyso-Keima
author: Vinay V. Eapen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx8qprvw
materials: Select the singlets by gating SSC-A with SSC-W(width).

steps.title: Produce lentivirus in HEK293T
steps.instruction: Co‑transfect HEK293T cells with pPAX2, pMD2, and the mKeima‑tagged Galectin‑3 vector at a 4:2:1 mass ratio using polyethylenimine (PEI).

steps.title: Harvest and filter viral supernatant
steps.instruction: Two days post‑transfection, collect the virus‑containing supernatant, filter it through a 0.22 µm syringe filter, and add polybrene to a final concentration of 8 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Infect target cells and select
steps.instruction: Infect the target cell line with varying amounts of the filtered virus, then select stably transduced cells with puromycin (1 mg mL⁻¹ for HeLa; adjust for other lines). Verify expression by flow cytometry or confocal imaging; if expression is low, sort Keima‑positive cells by FACS.

steps.title: Expand stable Keima‑Galectin‑3 cells
steps.instruction: Grow the puromycin‑selected cells to 50–70 % confluency in 6‑well plates, preparing triplicate wells for each condition.

steps.title: Plate cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Seed the stable Keima‑Galectin‑3 cells into appropriate culture vessels (e.g., 6‑well plates) and allow them to reach 50–70 % confluency before treatment.

steps.title: Treat cells with LLoMe
steps.instruction: Add LLoMe to a final concentration of 500 µM – 1 mM and incubate for exactly 01:00:00 (1 h). Adjust the dose empirically for each cell line as needed.

steps.title: Add Bafilomycin A1 control
steps.instruction: After the LLoMe incubation, remove the LLoMe‑containing medium, replace it with fresh medium lacking LLoMe, and add Bafilomycin A1 to a final concentration of 20 nM in one set of wells to serve as a negative control (blocks lysosomal acidification).

steps.title: Harvest cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: At the desired time point, detach cells with trypsin, pellet at 1 000 rpm at 4 °C for 00:03:00, resuspend in FACS buffer (1× PBS + 2 % FBS), filter through cell‑strainer caps into FACS tubes, keep on ice, and acquire ~10 000 events per replicate on a flow cytometer. Export data to FlowJo.

steps.title: Gate and analyze flow data
steps.instruction: In FlowJo, gate live cells using Side Scatter (Area‑SSC‑A) vs Forward Scatter (Area‑FSC‑A), then select singlets and plot Acidic Keima (Texas Red‑A) against Neutral Keima (BB630‑A) to identify Keima‑positive cells. Calculate the ratio of mean Acidic Keima signal to mean Neutral Keima signal; a shift toward higher acidic signal indicates lysophagic flux.

steps.title: Prepare lysates for western blot (optional)
steps.instruction: Collect cell pellets, resuspend in 8 M urea buffer (8 M urea, 150 mM Tris pH 7.4, 50 mM NaCl) supplemented with protease and phosphatase inhibitors.

substeps.instruction: Determine protein concentration with Bradford or BCA assay.
Boil equal amounts of lysate in 1× SDS Laemmli buffer; use at least 10–15 µg protein per lane.

steps.title: Run and detect western blot (optional)
steps.instruction: Separate proteins on 4–20 % Tris‑Glycine gels (Bio‑Rad), transfer wet onto PVDF membranes, and probe with α‑Keima antibody diluted 1:1000 in 5 % milk TBST. Visualize with enhanced chemiluminescence (film or digital). Processed Keima runs at ~25 kDa; full‑length Keima‑Galectin‑3 at ~50 kDa.

steps.title: Plate cells on glass‑bottom dishes for imaging
steps.instruction: Seed stable Keima‑Galectin‑3 cells onto 35 mm glass‑bottom dishes (MatTek, No. 1.5, 14 mm diameter) and grow to 50–70 % confluency in DMEM high‑glucose, pyruvate, +10 % FBS.

steps.title: Treat and washout cells for imaging
steps.instruction: Treat the plated cells with 500 µM – 1 mM LLoMe for 01:00:00, then replace with phenol‑red‑free FluoroBrite DMEM +10 % FBS. Add Bafilomycin A1 (20 nM) to the control wells. Proceed after the defined washout interval.

steps.title: Acquire ratiometric confocal images
steps.instruction: Image cells at 37 °C on a Yokogawa CSU‑X1 spinning‑disk confocal mounted on a Nikon Ti‑E microscope (Harvard Imaging Center) using the Perfect Focus System. Use a 40×/1.30 NA or 100×/1.40 NA objective. Sequentially excite with 100 mW 442 nm and 100 mW 561 nm lasers, collect emission through a 620/60 nm filter, and capture with a Hamamatsu ORCA‑ER cooled CCD (6.45 µm² pixel) controlled by MetaMorph.

steps.title: Generate maximum‑projection images
steps.instruction: Create maximum‑intensity Z‑projections of each channel stack and save the projections using Fiji (ImageJ).

steps.title: Quantify acidic Keima puncta
steps.instruction: In CellProfiler, divide the 561‑nm channel by the 442‑nm channel (Image Math) to obtain a ratio image. Identify primary objects with an Otsu threshold, selecting puncta 5–20 pixels in diameter. Relate each puncta to its parent cell and count.

steps.title: Prepare images for publication
steps.instruction: For each channel stack, adjust brightness and contrast equally, convert to RGB, and apply a “Fire” lookup table to the ratio image (acidic signal) in Fiji. Export the RGB images for figure assembly.
